boards.title: Your First Weekend at Spelman College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend route through named Spelman landmarks, campus resources, art, and wellness spaces.

cards.title: Start at West Campus Parking Deck
cards.subtitle: Arrival point on Spelman’s campus map
cards.notes: Use the campus map to orient yourself at the West Campus Parking Deck, then follow Public Safety directions before setting out on foot.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a map-based campus orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman’s campus map lists the West Campus Parking Deck and Public Safety as location 1.
cards.access_notes: Visitors should follow directions from Public Safety at the campus gates.

cards.title: Have a campus meal at Alma Upshaw
cards.subtitle: Albert Manley Student Center, second floor
cards.notes: Plan a meal stop at Alma Upshaw Dining Hall in the Albert Manley Student Center; bring your Spelman ID for dining transactions.
cards.short_summary: A practical early stop for a meal on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman identifies Alma Upshaw Dining Hall on the second floor of the Albert Manley Student Center and requires a Spelman ID for dining transactions.
cards.access_notes: Dining transactions require the cardholder’s Spelman ID.

cards.title: Settle in at Woodruff Library
cards.subtitle: Atlanta University Center Consortium library
cards.notes: Take time to locate research help, collections, and study areas at the AUC Woodruff Library, which serves Spelman and AUC partner institutions.
cards.short_summary: Make the shared AUC library part of your campus bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Robert W. Woodruff AUC Library supports Spelman and three other AUC institutions and is the consortium’s intellectual and information hub.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current service information before visiting.

cards.title: Pause at Grover-Werden Memorial Fountain
cards.subtitle: Center of the campus oval
cards.notes: Walk to the campus oval for a brief outdoor pause at the Grover-Werden Memorial Fountain and read its role in Spelman’s campus history.
cards.short_summary: A historic landmark for an outdoor campus pause.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman’s student handbook says the Grover-Werden Memorial Fountain, dedicated in 1927, is located in the center of the campus oval.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; respect any posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Find Rockefeller Hall
cards.subtitle: Historic Spelman campus building
cards.notes: Add Rockefeller Hall to your walking route and notice its place in Spelman’s built history before continuing toward nearby campus landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman’s student handbook identifies Rockefeller Hall as the oldest building on campus, completed in 1886.
cards.access_notes: Use exterior viewing and follow building-access rules.

cards.title: Walk by Sisters Chapel
cards.subtitle: Historic chapel on Spelman’s campus map
cards.notes: Include Sisters Chapel on the landmark loop. Check campus programming separately if you want to attend an event rather than view the building.
cards.short_summary: A historic chapel connected to Spelman’s founding story.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman’s student handbook states that Sisters Chapel was built in 1927 and is named for Laura Spelman Rockefeller and Lucy Maria Spelman.
cards.access_notes: Use exterior viewing unless an event or campus access policy permits entry.

cards.title: Get acquainted with the Wellness Center
cards.subtitle: Wellness Center at Read Hall
cards.notes: Stop by the Wellness Center at Read Hall to identify the pool, indoor track, MAC Courts, and other facilities available to the campus community.
cards.short_summary: Locate recreation and wellness resources for later use.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman says the Wellness Center at Read Hall includes MAC Courts, a heated pool, indoor track, cycling room, multipurpose rooms, and teaching kitchen.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and hours can change; check the Wellness Center’s current information.

cards.entity_name: Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts
cards.title: Explore the CI&A’s public-facing spaces
cards.subtitle: Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts
cards.notes: Walk to the CI&A and look for its arts, innovation, and community-facing spaces; consult current programming before entering specialized areas.
cards.short_summary: A newer center connecting arts, technology, and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman describes the Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts as a cross-disciplinary learning environment that unites artistic expression and technology.
cards.source_title: Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts
cards.access_notes: Some spaces or programs may have campus-specific access requirements.

cards.title: Look for the Bank of America Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor of the Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current exhibition information, then visit the Bank of America Gallery in the CI&A as part of your arts-focused campus walk.
cards.short_summary: Pair an art stop with the new CI&A building.
cards.evidence_claim: Spelman identifies the Bank of America Gallery as a Museum of Fine Art location on the first floor of the Mary Schmidt Campbell Center for Innovation & the Arts.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — Spelman College Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: The Museum lists Bank of America Gallery hours as Wednesday–Friday, 1–5 p.m.; Saturdays are by appointment only.

cards.entity_name: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art — Cosby Gallery
cards.title: End with the Museum’s Cosby Gallery
cards.subtitle: Camille Olivia Hanks Cosby, Ed.D. Academic Center, first floor
cards.notes: Finish with the Museum’s Cosby Gallery. Review the current exhibition and visitor guidelines, including its no-food rule and no-flash photography request.
cards.short_summary: A free public art stop with current exhibition programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spelman College Museum of Fine Art states that admission is free and open to the public; Cosby Gallery is on the first floor of the Cosby Academic Center.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — Spelman College Museum of Fine Art
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are Wednesday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m.; it is closed during Spelman College breaks.
